clue.text: Reason for meltwater possibly submerging large riverbed's course

indicators.note: to submerge something is to put it under the surface, so one piece goes down inside another

parts.note: a thaw is what makes ice and snow turn to meltwater
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
e.g. offers a possible instance, so 'possibly' can stand for it

explanation.surface: A glaciologist explains how a big spring thaw floods and reshapes the bed of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the thaw as only one example of a cause, which is why it supplies EG; L stands for large as on clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalweg is the line joining the deepest points along a river channel, the path its main current follows.

clue.text: Set up to collect rat hormone in pregnancy

indicators.note: collecting something means gathering it in, so one piece is held inside the other
in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a lot is a set of items sold together at auction
a heel is a contemptible person, a rat

explanation.surface: A lab technician rigs a trap to capture a rat in order to measure its pregnancy hormones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the laboratory animal from the surface, but here it is a scoundrel, and 'set' is an auction lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Theelol is an old name for oestriol, an oestrogen produced in large quantities by the placenta during gestation.

clue.text: Not a conventional device with a grave lack of disk capacity?

parts.note: taken as written
a tomb is a grave
a lack is nothing, zero, the letter O
megabytes, abbreviated MB, measure how much a disk holds

explanation.surface: A tech reviewer sneers at an odd gadget whose drive has almost no storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about computer kit, but 'device' here is a weapon, and 'a grave' and 'lack of disk capacity' assemble A TOMB, O, MB. Weapons that are not nuclear are called conventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Military language divides weapons into conventional and nuclear, and a fission bomb is the classic nuclear, unconventional weapon.

clue.text: 17th-century corporation's capital losses from sheep (mother and young)

indicators.note: capitals are the opening letters, and losing them means each word gives up its first letter

parts.note: a ewe is a mother sheep
a lamb is a young sheep

explanation.surface: A company of the 1600s writes off losses on a flock of ewes and lambs.
explanation.walkthrough: EWE and LAMB each lose their capital letter, leaving WE and AMB. 'Corporation' is humorous slang for a paunch, which is the sense needed, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Weamb is an obsolete spelling of womb, which once also meant belly, and corporation is jocular slang for a big stomach.

clue.text: Philistinism singer Turner raised in concert that wows me

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance

indicators.note: placing one piece in another puts it inside

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise or admiration

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters makes them read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: Tina Turner, the American singer

explanation.surface: A snobbish critic sniffs at Tina Turner being lifted up on stage at a show that thrilled them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That wows me' seems to describe the concert, but it is a standalone exclamation of surprise, which the reversed singer splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigmanity is Carlyle's coinage for the smug, respectable middle class, the outlook of people with no taste for culture.

clue.text: I messed up greeting in wrestling ring

parts.note: 'D'oh!' is Homer Simpson's cry on realising a blunder
'yo' is an informal hello

explanation.surface: A wrestler admits fluffing the ritual bow on entering the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I messed up' reads as a confession in the scene, but it is the exclamation DOH, followed by the greeting YO.
explanation.definitionFit: The dohyo is the raised clay circle in which sumo bouts are fought.

clue.text: Nobleman and tasty swimmer converge, expressing their shared ecstasy for spicy nut mix

indicators.note: to express is to squeeze out, so a letter is pressed out of the middle

parts.note: a duke is a high-ranking noble

indicators.note: two things converging travel towards each other, so the second runs the opposite way to the first

parts.note: hake is an edible sea fish
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, and it ends one word and starts the other once they meet

explanation.surface: A lord and a fish meet in a moment of mutual rapture over a bowl of spiced nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: DUKE runs forwards and HAKE comes back to meet it as EKAH; they overlap on the shared E, which is then squeezed out, leaving DUK plus KAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukkah is an Egyptian blend of toasted nuts, seeds and spices, used as a dip with bread and oil.

clue.text: Moth ruined kit, invading skirt's frame

indicators.note: an invader goes inside territory, so one piece enters another

parts.note: a hoop is the stiff ring that holds out a hooped skirt

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper form, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A moth has chewed through someone's gear and got into the frame of a crinoline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moth' is the definition at the front, not the culprit that ruined the kit; a hoop is the ring frame of a crinoline skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hook-tips are moths of the family Drepanidae, named for the hooked points of their forewings.

clue.text: American has a quality like this, going over or next to staff?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means turning upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
a thing that has a quality like this one 'is so'

explanation.surface: An American score annotation, placed above or beside the stave, seems to describe itself.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus IS SO reads AISSO, which turns over to give the answer. 'Staff' is the musical stave, and 'over or next to' describes where the alternative passage is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossia is Italian for 'or', marking an alternative, often easier, passage printed above or beside the main stave.

clue.text: Vehicle user's first to clip tailless breed of sheep or deer

indicators.note: an animal without a tail has lost its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the Jacob is a piebald, many-horned sheep breed

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A motorist clips a stubby-tailed sheep or a deer on a country road.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR, then JACOB without its tail, with the U clipped on the end. 'Breed of sheep or deer' reads as one phrase, but 'deer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The carjacou is the Virginian or white-tailed deer of North America, an old name taken from a native word.

clue.text: Point in a circle, dispatching The Last of Us's cordyceps victim

indicators.note: dispatching means sending away, so a letter is removed
in places the compass point inside the a-and-circle pair

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
west is a compass point

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here the end of Us's

parts.note: the word whose final letter is sent away

explanation.surface: A nod to the video game The Last of Us, whose zombie fungus is cordyceps, with a compass point inside a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: WEST goes inside A and O to make AWESTO; 'dispatching' then removes S, the last letter of 'Us's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aweto is a New Zealand caterpillar killed and mummified by a Cordyceps fungus, once used as a source of tattoo pigment.

clue.text: Actor Tom forgoing lead villain in Wall Street gets into Medicine Man and others

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it
to forgo the lead is to give up the front position, so the opening letter is lost

parts.note: Tom Hanks, the Hollywood star
Gordon Gekko is the ruthless financier in the film Wall Street

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actor turns down the villain's part in Wall Street and takes roles in Medicine Man and similar films.
explanation.walkthrough: Medicine Man is a 1992 Sean Connery film, which fits the movie surface, but here it is the definition, an Inuit shaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An angekok is an Inuit shaman or sorcerer, a healer and spirit-mediator, so the plural covers medicine men generally.

clue.text: Islamic robe of judge in the style of loose vest

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
à la is French for in the manner of
a bib is the loose sleeveless vest worn over kit in team sports

explanation.surface: A judge's gown is described as cut like a baggy vest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a bib is also the coloured mesh tabard used to mark teams in training, the loose vest wanted here.
explanation.definitionFit: Jalabib is the plural of jilbab, the long loose outer garment worn by some Muslim women.

clue.text: Eg film evoking sorrow turns on auteur's introduction to the stars

indicators.note: something that turns round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: film is one example of an art form
something that evokes sorrow is sad

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A melancholy film turns on its director's opening shot of the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Ad Astra is also a 2019 space film, a pleasing echo of the surface, but the definition is the Latin phrase; 'on' sets the reversed part after the initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad astra is Latin, used in mottoes such as 'per ardua ad astra', meaning towards the heavens.

clue.text: Not exactly a cracking nut wrapped with citrus fruit

parts.note: c., short for circa, means approximately

indicators.note: cracking a shell breaks it apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an almond is a nut
someone wrapped in a coat is in it

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely describes a cracked nut packaged with a piece of citrus.
explanation.walkthrough: C for circa, A, the cracked ALMOND rearranged to LAMOND, then IN for wrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The calamondin is a small, sour orange-like fruit from the Philippines, a hybrid of mandarin and kumquat.

clue.text: Foolishness upended use as an example for party to follow

indicators.note: turning something end over end puts its bottom at the top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to model a thing on another is to use it as a pattern
a do is a party
on means further along, coming after, as in 'later on'

explanation.surface: Someone turns an example on its head to justify a party.
explanation.walkthrough: MODEL, DO and ON are strung together and the whole is turned upside down in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a simpleton, and the suffix -dom makes a state or realm, so this is the condition of being a fool.

clue.text: Lower House occupant initiates viral complaint

indicators.note: to initiate is to begin, so this piece comes at the start, ahead of the other

parts.note: a Member of Parliament sits in the House of Commons
something that lows, as cattle do, is a lower

explanation.surface: A backbencher in the Commons starts a complaint that goes viral online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower House' reads as the Commons, but the split is 'Lower', a mooing beast, and 'House occupant'. The Commons is the lower house of Britain's Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Mpox is the current name for monkeypox, an infectious disease caused by a virus related to smallpox.

clue.text: King ascending, once grotesque, is drying up

indicators.note: in a down entry, ascending means climbing from the bottom, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
antic meant grotesque or bizarre in older English

explanation.surface: A monarch, formerly freakish, rises to the throne as his powers wither.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' flags the obsolete sense of ANTIC, which today means playful or capering.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerantic comes from Greek xeros, dry, and describes something that dries out or causes drying.

clue.text: Plant that flowers on and off, on and off, between tense and not tense

indicators.note: between puts the alternate letters inside the tense and not-tense pieces

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
lax means slack, the opposite of tense

indicators.note: on and off means intermittently, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the words whose alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A botanical riddle about a plant flowering intermittently, somewhere between taut and slack.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'on and off' is the fodder: its first, third, fifth and seventh letters give OADF, which sits between T and LAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadflax is a flowering plant of the snapdragon family, with yellow spurred blooms.

clue.text: Player of Flute needs this Shakespearean din to stop flat

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so the wanted piece is what fills the middle of the shorter word

parts.note: a flutist plays the flute
Flt is the abbreviation for flat in addresses

explanation.surface: An amateur actor cast as Flute in A Midsummer Night's Dream needs a racket to drown out a flat note.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: FLT stopped with the answer gives FLUTIST, so the answer is what remains of FLUTIST when FLT is taken away. Flute is a character in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a pleasing decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Utis is an old word for noisy revelry or uproar, used by Shakespeare in Henry IV Part 2.

clue.text: People ruled by Mercury retrograde under current line of constant declination

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece under another is placed after it

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: a retrograde planet appears to move backwards, so the letters run the wrong way

parts.note: in astrology Mercury is the ruling planet of Virgo

explanation.surface: An astrologer warns star signs ruled by Mercury about its retrograde phase.
explanation.walkthrough: The astrological picture is apt: 'retrograde' really is said of Mercury, here turning VIRGOS round beneath the I.
explanation.definitionFit: An isogriv is a navigation chart line joining points with equal grid variation, the angle between grid north and magnetic north.

clue.text: Shaker was one local to shout, getting parrot back inside

indicators.note: to get something is to take it into your possession, so one piece is taken into the other
inside spells out where the taken piece ends up, within the other

parts.note: holler is a regional, chiefly American, word for shout

indicators.note: going back means running the opposite way, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A cocktail shaker was used by a local to make a racket while their parrot came home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaker' looks like a cocktail shaker or a mover, but it is a member of the Shakers, the ecstatic religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy roller is a mocking name for a member of a sect given to frenzied, physically ecstatic worship, as the Shakers were.

clue.text: Deceptively fluent (but not good) formal poet one spotted in bestiary?

indicators.note: 'not good' means without the abbreviation for good, so that letter is struck out

parts.note: glib speech is smooth but shallow or insincere
bard is the elevated word for a poet

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking, stiff poet is noticed in a medieval book of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'noticed' but describes the animal's coat; G is the usual abbreviation for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Libbard is an archaic form of leopard, the spotted big cat that appears in medieval bestiaries.

clue.text: Apish attempt to call using phone card for days

indicators.note: using one thing for another means putting it in that other's place

parts.note: to dial a number is to try to ring someone
a SIM card goes in a mobile phone
d is the abbreviation for days

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily tries to make a call, monkeying about with the card in their phone.
explanation.walkthrough: In DIAL, the D for days is swapped for SIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Simial is a rare adjective from Latin simia, ape, so it means resembling or relating to apes.

clue.text: Jointly sung about one of films covering early developers?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: choral music is sung by a choir together
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A song performed together about a film on the pioneers of early cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' suggests cinema and 'early developers' photographers, but the films are membranes and the developers are embryos.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorial relates to the chorion, the outermost membrane enclosing the embryo of reptiles, birds and mammals.

clue.text: Box office's opening with free entry to Americans

parts.note: to cuff someone is to box their ears, to hit them

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A theatre box office opens with admission at no charge for American visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box office' reads as one thing, but 'Box' is the verb hit and 'office' supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuffo is American slang meaning gratis, especially of admission to a show without paying.

clue.text: Gold dress like leather worn by ornithologist

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to dub leather is to dress it with grease to make it supple
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A bird expert turns up in a golden outfit that looks like leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' reads as a garment, but here it is the verb used of treating leather.
explanation.definitionFit: John James Audubon was the American naturalist famed for his painted studies of North American birds.

clue.text: Radical group that supports Liberal

parts.note: an ally is one who backs you
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A militant political faction declares its backing for the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' looks political, but it is the chemist's term for a group of atoms acting as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry allyl is the C3H5 unit, a radical or substituent found in compounds like allyl alcohol.

clue.text: Fine old bird lumbered with a historical ban

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: to lumber is to move clumsily, so the letters stumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine imposed on an elderly person who is saddled with an ancient prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lumbered with' reads as burdened with, but 'lumbered' is the anagram signal for the following words, with 'a' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbiddal is an obsolete noun meaning prohibition, the act of forbidding something.

clue.text: A rial isn't right money for the Maldives

indicators.note: something not right is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a rial is the wrong currency to use in the Maldives.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is plausible advice: the rial is Iranian or Gulf money, and its letters rearranged give the right coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The laari is a subunit of the Maldivian rufiyaa, one hundredth of it.

clue.text: Old challenger dismisses one ancient sage

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a rival challenges you
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A veteran challenger brushes aside a wise elder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' suggests a wise person, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Orval is an archaic name for clary, a plant of the genus Salvia, so a kind of sage the herb.

clue.text: Softened nuts coating starter of lamb chop

indicators.note: a coating covers the outside, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: nuts means crazy

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
to axe is to chop

explanation.surface: A cook softens a lamb chop starter under a crust of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'starter' read as kitchen words, but they mean crazy and first letter, and 'chop' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To malax is to knead or work a substance until it becomes soft and pliable.
